column1: # Locks the Python binding's functions take while they hold the GIL.
# Read by scripts/check/c/snapshot-getters.sh (check 2), which fails on any
# such lock not listed here AND on any row whose function no longer takes it.
# Columns (TAB-separated): path, Type::function (bare name for a free
# function), lock, reason. The lock is the identifier the lock call is made on
# header says how it is found): a row allows that one lock in that function,
# so a second lock taken there with the GIL held is reported on its own.
# A row is a claim about the LOCK, not only the function: no holder of it
# keeps the guard while the GIL is released. If one did, it would need the GIL
# back before the guard could drop, and a function listed here — waiting for
# the guard with the GIL held — would freeze the interpreter. The reason names
# the lock and says why that cannot happen; re-check every row that shares the
# A listed function also runs no Python code while it holds the guard: it
# ...), reads no caller's object (`extract`, `getattr`) and drops no Python
# object. Python code can hand the GIL to a thread that then waits for the
# same lock with the GIL held. Take the value out, let the guard drop, then
# build the error. The scan does not check this; review does.
# Not a candidate for this list — fix the function instead:
#   - the lock is held across `py.detach` anywhere (a push, a send, a
#     recv): take it inside `detach` and raise after the GIL is back;
#   - the value cannot change after construction: capture it at construction;
